# model-context-stream

> MIT-licensed, self-hostable MCP server that keeps fleets of AI agents mutually
> context-aware: durable, replayable context streams backed by Redis Streams, a task
> queue with exactly-once claims and crash-safe leases, versioned protocols
> (playbooks), agent presence, HTTP ingest, and HMAC-signed outbound webhooks —
> served over MCP Streamable HTTP.

Key facts:
- Any MCP client connects to http://<host>:3000/mcp with a bearer token; agents get
  tools like publish_event, read_stream (durable cursors, blockMs long-poll),
  create_task, claim_task, complete_task, get_protocol, and whoami.
- Task claims are atomic (Redis Lua) with exactly one winner, verified by a 25-way
  concurrent race test; leases return a crashed agent's task to the queue.
- Non-MCP systems publish via POST /ingest/:stream and read via GET /streams/:stream
  (plain HTTP, bearer auth, durable cursors) — no MCP session needed.
- The server never calls an LLM; stream compaction is agent-driven via digest tasks.
- Quickstart: two commands with prebuilt multi-arch images from GHCR
  (ghcr.io/thejavapirate/model-context-stream); production Helm chart at
  oci://ghcr.io/thejavapirate/charts/model-context-stream; Prometheus metrics at /metrics.
- Coordination state is Redis-backed and replica-safe (v0.4.0+).
